messages:
Olivia Chen: Quick follow-up from today's RFC review — I'm leaning toward the simplified handoff API (remove LeaseToken choreography, expose 'reserve/release' + optional sticky mode). Wanted to surface a few risks before we lock it in.

Kai Patel: I like the UX reduction but worried about fragmentation on long-lived tenants. The LeaseToken dance gave us a natural backpressure signal for tenants that churn memory too slowly.

David Romero: +1 on the simplification for clarity. Measured some microbenchmarks on the branch that removes token handoffs:
```
bench_offload --seq=2048 --batch=64
median latency: +6%
p95: +12%
cost per token: -15%
```
So cost improves but tails widen in heavy-multiplex scenarios.

Maria Gonzales: Could we keep a lightweight soft-reserve flag for pinned allocations instead of full tokens? Something like:
```
reserve_allocation(id, mode="sticky"|"ephemeral")
release(id)
// optional: set demote_after_ms=120000
```
Default ephemeral, sticky only for explicit pin. Keeps surface small.

Kai Patel: Sticky helps for hot parameters but it trades off unit utilization. If too many stickies, latency spiral. We need a demotion policy (age + access frequency) and a global admission limiter so tenants can't rathole memory. Also consider a per-tenant frag budget.

Olivia Chen: Proposal: default ephemeral, sticky opt-in; add eviction-notify webhook + telemetry so SDKs can retry smarter. Rollout plan: canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with regression gates (p95, cost-per-token, fragmentation metric).

infra-bot: scheduled deploy: feature-flag memory.handoff.simplified -> canary group 1 on Mon 09:00 UTC. Monitoring dashboards: /d/memory/handoff-simplified (owner: @maria).

David Romero: One more: model warmups rely on KV cache and soft residency. If we offload aggressively we'll pay recompute costs. Suggest keeping recent prefixes cached with TTL-based heuristics (e.g., keep last 2 minutes of KV per-model). In our perf tests that reduces p95 regressions from +12% -> +3%.

Maria Gonzales: I'll draft the follow-up RFC addressing: API samples, demotion heuristics, sticky opt-in semantics, TTL cache defaults, and rollout/metric gates. Action items: Maria write RFC, Kai run fragmentation sim across mixed tenant traces, David add scavenger/coalesce prototype for eviction, Olivia own rollout gating and docs.

Kai Patel: I'll run frag sims this week. Any preferred datasets? Suggest: mix of chat, embedding-only, and long-context batch workloads.

David Romero: Use the tenant traces from Q4 replay set + the new synthetic heavy-tail generator I checked in (tools/tracegen/heavy_tail). I'll wire a harness to measure rewarm cost.

Olivia Chen: Sounds good. Quick ask: keep the initial canary conservative on sticky allocations (disable sticky by FF until we have demotion).

Maria Gonzales: noted. I'll include explicit knobs for FF and per-tenant quotas in the RFC.

Olivia Chen: ok thanks — please ping this thread when the RFC is up, we'll schedule a 30m follow-up if there are open design gaps. :+1:

David Romero: +1

Kai Patel: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy canary created (id: canary-2026-04-12-01).
